title: Semolina Pudding
subtitle: Creamy, warm pudding of fine semolina cooked in sweet milk
excerpt: Fine wheat semolina whisked into hot sweetened milk and cooked for 12 minutes until thick, smooth, and creamy. The quickest of the British milk puddings and one of the most forgiving.
sourceNotes: Semolina pudding is the simplest of the British milk puddings, grain, milk, sugar. Mrs Beeton included it as one of the quickest puddings a home cook could make. It was a school dinner staple through the mid-20th century and is now somewhat unfashionable, which is undeserved, properly made, it is a gentle, comforting thing.

content.text: Semolina pudding is fine wheat grain whisked into hot sweetened milk and stirred over a medium-low heat until thick and smooth. It is one of the quickest milk puddings, ready in about 15 minutes from cold, and among the most forgiving: if it gets too thick, add more milk; if too thin, cook a little longer. A grating of nutmeg over the top is traditional and worth doing.

items.prepNote: a pinch, freshly grated, to serve

content.text: Pour the milk into a medium saucepan and heat over a medium heat until it is steaming and just beginning to bubble at the edges, not a rolling boil, just hot. Add the sugar and stir to dissolve.

Sprinkle the semolina into the hot milk in a thin, steady stream, whisking constantly as you pour. If you add it all at once, lumps form immediately. Once the semolina is all incorporated and the mixture is smooth, reduce the heat to medium-low.

Stir steadily with a wooden spoon or silicone spatula for 10 to 12 minutes until the pudding has thickened to a creamy, smooth consistency that falls from the spoon in a slow, heavy ribbon. It should hold its shape briefly in the bowl before settling. Remove from the heat.

Stir in the vanilla extract and the butter until the butter has melted and the pudding is glossy. Pour immediately into warm bowls and grate nutmeg generously over the top. Serve at once, semolina sets firm very quickly as it cools.

items.cause: The semolina was added to the milk too quickly or all at once.
items.fix: Add in a thin, slow stream while whisking. If lumps have formed, pass the pudding through a sieve and return to the pan to finish cooking.

items.symptom: The pudding is too thick and stiff
items.cause: Cooked too long, or proportion of semolina to milk was slightly high.
items.fix: Stir in more hot milk, a little at a time, until it loosens to the right consistency.

items.symptom: The pudding has set solid in the bowl before it could be eaten
items.cause: Semolina sets very fast once off the heat.
items.fix: Serve into warm bowls immediately, as soon as it leaves the pan. There is no way to slow the setting, so serve quickly.

content.text: Best eaten immediately. Semolina sets very firm on cooling and the texture changes. Leftovers can be sliced and fried in butter, or thinned with hot milk over low heat.
